stem: At a postpartum follow-up visit, a client reports feeling persistently overwhelmed and no longer enjoying activities that were previously pleasurable. Which nursing action best supports safe psychosocial adaptation to parenthood?

options.A: Use a standardized, validated depression/anxiety screening instrument and ensure abnormal results receive timely assessment and follow-up
options.B: Reassure the client that all mood changes after birth are normal and do not require screening
options.C: Focus only on the newborn because parental emotional health is outside postpartum care
options.D: Advise the client to wait until symptoms have lasted several months before discussing them with a clinician

rationale: ACOG recommends screening people receiving postpartum care for depression and anxiety with standardized, validated instruments and implementing screening within a system that provides timely assessment, diagnosis, treatment, monitoring, and follow-up based on severity. Persistent loss of pleasure and feeling overwhelmed warrant assessment rather than normalization or delay. Parental mental health is an integral part of postpartum care. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Support postpartum psychosocial adaptation by screening for depression and anxiety with a validated tool and ensuring timely follow-up when symptoms or screening results are concerning.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
source_document_title: Patient Screening — Perinatal Mental Health; Optimizing Postpartum Care
source_version_date: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 4 framework (June 2023) and current implementation guidance; pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Patient Screening: screen everyone receiving postpartum care for depression and anxiety using standardized validated instruments; screening must be paired with systems for timely assessment, diagnosis, treatment, monitoring and follow-up. Optimizing Postpartum Care > Mood and emotional well-being: screen for postpartum depression/anxiety with a validated instrument and provide support/resources
source_claim_supported: Postpartum mental-health symptoms should be assessed with validated depression/anxiety screening and positive/concerning findings should lead to timely follow-up rather than reassurance or delay.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — assess psychosocial status, identify mental-health concerns, provide emotional support, and facilitate appropriate referrals/resources
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — postpartum mental health / parental role adaptation
correction_summary: Replaced the generic statement about education and emotional support with a specific, evidence-based postpartum psychosocial assessment action. Used current ACOG guidance and made follow-up after abnormal screening part of the correct response.
audit_findings: A directly reflects ACOG recommendations. B normalizes potentially clinically important symptoms; C falsely excludes parental mental health from postpartum care; D delays indicated assessment. The item does not diagnose postpartum depression from the vignette alone and does not invent a symptom-duration threshold. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
